name: ordinary-branch-foundation-v1
question: How much opponent-reply breadth is required to preserve ordinary root decisions, and how do forcing, capture, random, and Locked-3 orderings compare at equal retained-reply budgets?
status: frozen before new ordinary branch-oracle probing
source: The 240 deterministic positions frozen and used as development in Experiment 014, grouped across 80 completed games and 40 opening/opponent pairs
development_guardrail: All source games and positions are permanently development-only for Branch-Law Discovery and cannot support a later confirmation claim
candidate_scope: Every legal root candidate is retained; Experiment 016 varies opponent replies only
oracle: Stockfish 18, one thread, 16 MB hash, 20000 nodes, all-legal MultiPV, new-game boundary per context
stability_oracle: Deterministic outcome-free SHA samples are repeated at 80000 nodes
records: root candidate desirability, rank, and 10/25/50/100-cp viability
candidate-value consequence of omitting each reply
root-decision consequence of omitting each reply
node role, root candidate, path, source game, and grouping context
baselines: current forcing priority plus lexical fill
oracle reply ordering as a nondeployable reference
all legal replies as the endpoint
primary_curve: fraction of opponent replies retained to root decision preservation within 25 cp
guardrails: absolute root regret for full-reference and pruned choices
oracle stability at four times the node budget
selector operations, latency, and retained branches
advancement: No learned selector may be trained or advanced in Experiment 016
